turns.assessment: The S24 transmitter raised EQPT_TX_FAIL exactly when the S21 far-end receiver lost och67. Subsequent loss of that same channel at every OCM along S24→S08→S23→S06→S21 confirms failure at or immediately after the S24 channel source, while unchanged aggregate amplifier telemetry and unaffected neighboring channels argue strongly against a span or amplifier failure. A local TX laser failure best fits; a full card failure is less likely because receiver-side monitoring at trx.och67.z did not become invalid.

proposals.rationale: The local EQPT_TX_FAIL alarm coincides with far-end OCH_LOS and complete loss of och67 along the S24-to-S21 route. This is the documented signature of the S24 transmit laser turning off or failing.

A card failure could also remove the transmitted channel, but it should additionally take down the unit's receive traffic and make its monitoring silent; unchanged receiver-side telemetry at trx.och67.z weighs against it.

Severe channel-specific attenuation at the S24 outgoing ROADM could make och67 disappear downstream without changing aggregate amplifier power, but it does not naturally explain the transmitter-specific equipment alarm.
